schema_description: openEHR Access Control: a draft change proposal for two concrete ACCESS_CONTROL_SETTINGS schemes carried by EHR_ACCESS (the controller's confidentiality and exclusions, and the access directives of consent, restriction, opt-out, delegation and labels that inherit them), a versioned ACCESS_POLICY of a controller with its care relationship facts, and versioned party relationships. The classes hold facts; the decision procedure is fixed by the scheme. Not an openEHR release.

CONFIDENTIALITY_SETTINGS.name: CONFIDENTIALITY_SETTINGS
CONFIDENTIALITY_SETTINGS.documentation: The concrete `ACCESS_CONTROL_SETTINGS` that holds the controller's facts about one EHR: the confidentiality of the whole record and the named parties excluded from it. The simplest concrete scheme; `ACCESS_DIRECTIVE_SETTINGS` inherits from it, so an EHR holds one settings object (`EHR_ACCESS._settings_` 0..1). `EHR_ACCESS.scheme()` returns `confidentiality` for an instance of this class.

marking.name: marking
marking.documentation: The confidentiality of the whole EHR. Void reads as `N`. Set only by the controller; a version committed by anyone else carries it unchanged.

exclusions.name: exclusions
exclusions.documentation: Denies the controller sets for this EHR alone, each of kind `exclusion` naming the parties it keeps out. Read and written only by the controller; a version committed by anyone else carries them unchanged.

scheme.name: scheme
scheme.documentation: The name of this scheme, `confidentiality`, which `EHR_ACCESS.scheme()` returns.

is_normal.name: is_normal
is_normal.documentation: True when `_marking_` is Void or its `level()` is 0.

CONFIDENTIALITY_MARKING.name: CONFIDENTIALITY_MARKING
CONFIDENTIALITY_MARKING.documentation: The confidentiality of a whole EHR or of one versioned object, with who set it, when and why. The levels are ordered `N` < `R` < `V`: a datum at a level is cleared by a permit that names that level or a higher one.

confidentiality.name: confidentiality
confidentiality.documentation: The confidentiality, coded in the `HL7_Confidentiality` code system (`N` normal, `R` restricted, `V` very restricted). The codes `U`, `L` and `M` of the same code system read as `N`.

set_by.name: set_by
set_by.documentation: The party that set this marking: the controller, or a professional acting for it.

reason.name: reason
reason.documentation: Why the marking was set, written for the subject to read. Never clinical content, and never read by an access decision.

level.name: level
level.documentation: The rank of `_confidentiality_` in the order the package fixes: 0 for `N` (and for `U`, `L` and `M`), 1 for `R`, 2 for `V`.

ACCESS_DIRECTIVE_SETTINGS.name: ACCESS_DIRECTIVE_SETTINGS
ACCESS_DIRECTIVE_SETTINGS.documentation: The access directive scheme, carried by `EHR_ACCESS._settings_` and versioned with the EHR. It inherits the controller's facts of `CONFIDENTIALITY_SETTINGS` and adds the facts the subject's instructions give: the default disposition, the gate-keepers who may change the settings, the directives the subject or their representative gave (consent, restriction, opt-out, delegation scope), and labels on individual versioned objects. It carries no rule language: the decision procedure that reads these facts is fixed by the scheme. `EHR_ACCESS.scheme()` returns `access_directives` for an instance of this class.

default_access.name: default_access
default_access.documentation: What the EHR admits where no directive applies, coded in the `access default` group: `open` (any caller the other layers admit), `restricted` (only callers a permit directive, a gate-keeper or a care relationship names) or `consent_required` (only callers a permit directive names, apart from the subject and an emergency override).

gate_keepers.name: gate_keepers
gate_keepers.documentation: The parties who may commit a new version of the `EHR_ACCESS` that holds these settings: usually `PARTY_SELF` for a competent adult, otherwise a parent, guardian or other responsible party referenced into the demographic service (BASE Architecture Overview, Security, Access Control of access settings). Empty leaves the change to the system's administrators.

directives.name: directives
directives.documentation: The directives in force or recorded for this EHR. A directive outside its `_time_validity_` is kept as history and decides nothing.

labels.name: labels
labels.documentation: Labels on individual versioned objects of the EHR, beside the labels the `ACCESS_POLICY` classifications give whole kinds of data and the marking of the whole EHR.

scheme.name: scheme
scheme.documentation: The name of this scheme, `access_directives`, which `EHR_ACCESS.scheme()` returns.

invariants.Directives_not_controller_rules: directives /= Void implies directives.for_all (d | not d.is_controller_rule and not d.is_exclusion and (d.exceptions = Void or d.exceptions.for_all (e | not e.is_controller_rule and not e.is_exclusion)))

ACCESS_DIRECTIVE.name: ACCESS_DIRECTIVE
ACCESS_DIRECTIVE.documentation: One instruction about access to the data of one EHR, given by the subject, their representative or the controller on their instruction: a consent permit or deny, an EHDS Art. 8 restriction, an EHDS Art. 10 opt-out, or the scope of a delegation; or one rule of a controller's `ACCESS_POLICY` for every EHR it keeps. A directive applies to an access when every attribute it sets matches the access (the actor, the operation, the purpose, the data, the time), and none of its exceptions applies. Where a permit and a deny both apply, the deny wins.

kind.name: kind
kind.documentation: What kind of instruction this is, coded in the `access directive kind` group: `consent`, `restriction`, `opt_out` or `delegation` for a directive of an EHR, `controller_rule` for a rule of an `ACCESS_POLICY`, `exclusion` for a controller's exclusion of a named party from one EHR (`CONFIDENTIALITY_SETTINGS._exclusions_`). The kind decides which callers the directive can bind and how a refusal is shown (a restriction and an opt-out read as absent).

effect.name: effect
effect.documentation: Whether the directive permits or denies the access it applies to, coded in the `access effect` group: `permit` or `deny`.

applies_to.name: applies_to
applies_to.documentation: The callers the directive applies to; any one matching scope is enough. Empty applies to every caller the kind can bind.

operations.name: operations
operations.documentation: The operations the directive applies to, coded in the draft `openehr_access` terminology's `access operation` group (`read`, `write`, `export`, `query`). Empty applies to every operation.

purposes.name: purposes
purposes.documentation: The purposes of use the directive applies to, coded in the purpose-of-use terminology the system accepts. Empty applies to every purpose. On a `controller_rule` it applies only to an access that declares one of them, since `ACCESS_POLICY.purpose_required` is the control for an access without one. On a directive of an EHR, a deny also covers an access that declares no purpose, which cannot show it is outside the deny.

data.name: data
data.documentation: The data the directive applies to; data in any one scope is covered. Empty applies to the whole EHR, including data recorded after the directive.

time_validity.name: time_validity
time_validity.documentation: When the directive is in force. Void is in force from the commit of the version that adds it until a later version removes it.

emergency_override.name: emergency_override
emergency_override.documentation: Whether a caller that invokes an emergency justification of the controller's policy is exempt from this directive (EHDS Art. 11(5) for a restriction; Art. 10(2) for an opt-out where national law allows it).

exceptions.name: exceptions
exceptions.documentation: Narrower directives of the opposite effect inside this one, such as 'deny mental health data, except to my GP'. An access an exception applies to is not decided by this directive.

instructed_by.name: instructed_by
instructed_by.documentation: Who gave the instruction: `PARTY_SELF` for the subject, otherwise their representative or the professional who recorded it on their behalf.

legal_grounds.name: legal_grounds
legal_grounds.documentation: The legal provisions the directive rests on, such as GDPR Art. 9(2)(a), EHDS Art. 8 or a national provision, coded in a terminology the jurisdiction names.

evidence.name: evidence
evidence.documentation: The record of the instruction in the EHR, such as the `ADMIN_ENTRY` that holds the signed consent (RM EHR IM, Entry package, Standard Clinical Types of Data).

identifiers.name: identifiers
identifiers.documentation: Identifiers of the directive in other systems, such as a FHIR `Consent.identifier`, an IHE BPPC or APPC policy identifier, or a national consent registry reference.

details.name: details
details.documentation: Further archetyped detail the deployment records with the directive. The decision procedure never reads it.

is_deny.name: is_deny
is_deny.documentation: True when `_effect_` is the `deny` code of the `access effect` group.

is_restriction.name: is_restriction
is_restriction.documentation: True when `_kind_` is the `restriction` code of the `access directive kind` group.

is_opt_out.name: is_opt_out
is_opt_out.documentation: True when `_kind_` is the `opt_out` code of the `access directive kind` group.

is_controller_rule.name: is_controller_rule
is_controller_rule.documentation: True when `_kind_` is the `controller_rule` code of the `access directive kind` group.

is_exclusion.name: is_exclusion
is_exclusion.documentation: True when `_kind_` is the `exclusion` code of the `access directive kind` group.

invariants.Exceptions_opposite: exceptions /= Void implies exceptions.for_all (e | e.is_deny /= is_deny and e.exceptions = Void)

ACCESS_ACTOR_SCOPE.name: ACCESS_ACTOR_SCOPE
ACCESS_ACTOR_SCOPE.documentation: A description of callers. A caller matches when it matches every attribute that is set.

party.name: party
party.documentation: A party in the demographic service: a `PERSON` or `AGENT` matches itself; an `ORGANISATION` or `GROUP` matches every caller that acts for it or is a member of it.

role.name: role
role.documentation: A role the caller performs: the caller matches when it is the `performer` of a `ROLE` in force (its `time_validity` holds the date of the access and its versioned object is not deleted) whose `name` (`PARTY.type()`) is a `DV_CODED_TEXT` with the same terminology and code, or when the verified credential of a caller from outside the system, admitted under an agreement, attests a professional role with the same terminology and code.

relationship.name: relationship
relationship.documentation: A relationship the caller must hold to the subject of the EHR, coded in the `access relationship` group: `care` (a live care relationship, narrowed by `_care_roles_` and `_care_path_`), `representative` or `proxy`.

care_roles.name: care_roles
care_roles.documentation: The roles in a care relationship the scope names: a caller matches when it holds a live care relationship to the subject whose `care_role` has the terminology and code of one of them. Void means any role. No role implies another.

care_path.name: care_path
care_path.documentation: How the care relationship reaches the caller, coded in the `care path` group: `direct`, `team`, `attested` or `self_declared`. Void means `direct` or `team`, and `attested` or `self_declared` only where the policy admits that path.

organisation_type.name: organisation_type
organisation_type.documentation: A type of organisation the caller acts for: the caller matches when it acts for an `ORGANISATION` whose `name` (`PARTY.type()`) is a `DV_CODED_TEXT` with the same terminology and code, or when the verified credential of a caller from outside the system, admitted under an agreement, attests a type of its healthcare facility with the same terminology and code.

caller_kind.name: caller_kind
caller_kind.documentation: The kind of caller, coded in the `access caller kind` group: `professional`, `access_service`, `subject`, `representative` or `system`.

invariants.Not_empty: party /= Void or role /= Void or organisation_type /= Void or relationship /= Void or caller_kind /= Void
invariants.Care_roles_valid: care_roles /= Void implies (not care_roles.is_empty and relationship /= Void and then relationship.defining_code.code_string.is_equal ("care"))
invariants.Care_path_valid: care_path /= Void implies (relationship /= Void and then relationship.defining_code.code_string.is_equal ("care") and terminology (Terminology_id_access).has_code_for_group_id (Group_id_access_care_path, care_path.defining_code))

ACCESS_DATA_SCOPE.name: ACCESS_DATA_SCOPE
ACCESS_DATA_SCOPE.documentation: A description of data in an EHR. Data match when they match every attribute that is set, and an attribute holding a list matches when any of its members does.

objects.name: objects
objects.documentation: Individual versioned objects, such as one `VERSIONED_COMPOSITION`.

templates.name: templates
templates.documentation: Template identifiers the data were committed under.

archetypes.name: archetypes
archetypes.documentation: Root archetypes of the data; a specialisation of a named archetype matches too.

categories.name: categories
categories.documentation: Categories of the data, such as the EHDS priority categories, coded in a terminology the jurisdiction names.

sensitivities.name: sensitivities
sensitivities.documentation: Sensitivity codes, matched against the labels the data carry, coded in a terminology the jurisdiction names (such as the `HL7_ActCode` sensitivity policy codes).

confidentialities.name: confidentialities
confidentialities.documentation: Confidentiality levels, coded in the `HL7_Confidentiality` code system (`N` normal, `R` restricted, `V` very restricted): the data whose confidentiality is one of these levels or a lower one.

origins.name: origins
origins.documentation: The systems the data came from, as `FEEDER_AUDIT_DETAILS._system_id_` or the committing system's `_system_id_` records them.

episodes.name: episodes
episodes.documentation: The episodes of care the data are placed in, each the `DV_IDENTIFIER` (`_issuer_` and `_id_`) of an `episode` element in the `_other_context_` of a composition's `EVENT_CONTEXT`, compared by issuer and id. Data placed in no episode match no entry.

invariants.Not_empty: objects /= Void or templates /= Void or archetypes /= Void or categories /= Void or sensitivities /= Void or confidentialities /= Void or origins /= Void or episodes /= Void or recorded /= Void
invariants.Confidentialities_valid: confidentialities /= Void implies (not confidentialities.is_empty and confidentialities.for_all (c | c.defining_code.terminology_id.value.is_equal (Terminology_id_confidentiality)))

ACCESS_LABEL.name: ACCESS_LABEL
ACCESS_LABEL.documentation: Labels on one versioned object of the EHR: sensitivity codes, a confidentiality, or both. A caller reads labelled data only when a permit clears every label, or an emergency override applies.

target.name: target
target.documentation: The versioned object the labels apply to.

sensitivities.name: sensitivities
sensitivities.documentation: The sensitivity codes the object carries.

confidentiality.name: confidentiality
confidentiality.documentation: The confidentiality of the object. The confidentiality of a datum is the highest of this marking, the marking of its EHR and the confidentiality its classifications give it.

reason.name: reason
reason.documentation: Why the object is labelled, never clinical content.

ACCESS_POLICY.name: ACCESS_POLICY
ACCESS_POLICY.documentation: The access policy of a system or of one controller in it: facts that hold for every EHR the controller keeps. It classifies kinds of data into sensitivities, states whether clinical access needs a care relationship and a declared purpose, holds the controller's own rules on which callers may perform which operations on which kinds of data, lists the named directives a subject can accept by reference, states what the subject's view of the access log withholds, and states how long the access log keeps an entry. Kept in its own versioned container, outside any EHR and outside the demographic service.

controller.name: controller
controller.documentation: The `ORGANISATION` whose policy this is, the controller of the data.

classifications.name: classifications
classifications.documentation: The rules that give kinds of data their sensitivity labels.

care_relationship_required.name: care_relationship_required
care_relationship_required.documentation: Whether a professional's clinical access to an EHR needs a live care relationship to its subject, beyond the operation the caller's capability grants.

relationship_grace.name: relationship_grace
relationship_grace.documentation: How long after a care relationship ends it still admits access, for follow-up (BASE Architecture Overview, Security, Time-limitation of access). Grace never extends a team membership.

time_zone.name: time_zone
time_zone.documentation: The time zone, as an IANA time zone name, in which the dates of a relationship's `time_validity` are read. Void means UTC.

care_purposes.name: care_purposes
care_purposes.documentation: The purposes of use for which a care relationship is a ground. Void means the `HL7_ActReason` codes `TREAT`, `ETREAT` and `CAREMGT`. An access that declares another purpose is not admitted by a relationship.

relationship_validity.name: relationship_validity
relationship_validity.documentation: The default and maximum periods of care relationships, by role and organisation type. A relationship no entry covers must be written with an end.

relationship_writers.name: relationship_writers
relationship_writers.documentation: The writers that may state a care relationship to a subject whose EHR is marked above `N`. Void means none.

team_targets.name: team_targets
team_targets.documentation: The `ORGANISATION` units a care relationship may name as its target. Void means none: a team target is then a `GROUP`.

self_declared_care.name: self_declared_care
self_declared_care.documentation: The longest period of a self-declared care relationship. Void means a self-declared relationship is refused at write.

attested_care.name: attested_care
attested_care.documentation: The agreements under which a caller's verified credential may attest a care relationship. Void means no attested relationship is admitted.

caseload.name: caseload
caseload.documentation: Whether a query may be narrowed to the caller's caseload and the caseload resource answers. Void means true.

episode_shared.name: episode_shared
episode_shared.documentation: The data every live care relationship of the controller covers whatever episode the relationship or the data name: the categories a professional reads across episodes, such as the patient summary. Void means none: placed data are covered only by a relationship of their episode or of none.

conflict_rules.name: conflict_rules
conflict_rules.documentation: The conflicts of interest the controller allows through the professional path. Void allows none: a professional who is the subject, or is related to the subject, is refused.

justifications.name: justifications
justifications.documentation: The grounds on which a caller is admitted outside its care relationships, by a declared purpose of use and a stated reason. Void admits nobody on a justification.

concealed_confidentialities.name: concealed_confidentialities
concealed_confidentialities.documentation: The confidentiality levels whose refused records are answered as absent. Void answers every refused named record as forbidden.

value_sets.name: value_sets
value_sets.documentation: The value sets the controller binds the coded attributes of care relationships, representations and rules to, held on a terminology server. A binding left out uses the default value set of the package.

purpose_required.name: purpose_required
purpose_required.documentation: Whether an access to clinical data must declare a purpose of use. An access without one is refused before the controller's rules are read, whatever rules the policy holds.

rules.name: rules
rules.documentation: The controller's rules for every EHR it keeps: which callers may perform which operations on which kinds of data, such as the rules a Member State lays down under EHDS Art. 11(3). Each is an `ACCESS_DIRECTIVE` of kind `controller_rule`. A deny rule that applies refuses whatever the subject's directives permit; a permit rule acts only on sensitivity, and a permit exception only narrows the deny rule it sits in.

catalogue.name: catalogue
catalogue.documentation: Named directives a subject can accept by an identifier, such as an IHE BPPC policy or a national consent choice. Each carries at least one identifier.

log_restrictions.name: log_restrictions
log_restrictions.documentation: The restrictions a Member State law lays on the subject's view of the access log under EHDS Article 9(3). Each names the kinds of accessor and the attributes of the accessor the subject view withholds; the full entry is unchanged.

log_retention.name: log_retention
log_retention.documentation: How long the access log keeps each entry, and the legal bounds the controller declares on that period. Void keeps every entry without end.

details.name: details
details.documentation: Further archetyped detail. The decision procedure never reads it.

invariants.Catalogue_identified: catalogue /= Void implies catalogue.for_all (d | d.identifiers /= Void)
invariants.Rules_kind: rules /= Void implies rules.for_all (r | r.is_controller_rule and (r.exceptions = Void or r.exceptions.for_all (e | e.is_controller_rule)))
invariants.Catalogue_not_controller_rules: catalogue /= Void implies catalogue.for_all (d | not d.is_controller_rule and not d.is_exclusion and (d.exceptions = Void or d.exceptions.for_all (e | not e.is_controller_rule and not e.is_exclusion)))
invariants.Team_targets_valid: team_targets /= Void implies (not team_targets.is_empty and team_targets.for_all (t | t.type.is_equal ("ORGANISATION")))
invariants.Concealed_valid: concealed_confidentialities /= Void implies (not concealed_confidentialities.is_empty and concealed_confidentialities.for_all (c | c.defining_code.terminology_id.value.is_equal (Terminology_id_confidentiality)))

ACCESS_CLASSIFICATION.name: ACCESS_CLASSIFICATION
ACCESS_CLASSIFICATION.documentation: One classification rule: data the scope describes carry the given sensitivity labels.

data.name: data
data.documentation: The kind of data the rule classifies. It names no individual object.

sensitivities.name: sensitivities
sensitivities.documentation: The sensitivity codes the data carry.

confidentiality.name: confidentiality
confidentiality.documentation: The confidentiality the data carry, coded in the `HL7_Confidentiality` code system (`N` normal, `R` restricted, `V` very restricted).

ACCESS_RELATIONSHIP_VALIDITY.name: ACCESS_RELATIONSHIP_VALIDITY
ACCESS_RELATIONSHIP_VALIDITY.documentation: The default and maximum period of the care relationships one entry covers. A relationship written without an end takes the default period from its start; one longer than the maximum is refused. An entry with neither period lets the relationships it covers stay open. An entry may also require the relationships it covers to name an episode of care.

roles.name: roles
roles.documentation: The `care_role` codes the entry covers. Void means every role.

organisation_types.name: organisation_types
organisation_types.documentation: The types of the relationship's `provider` the entry covers, matched as `ACCESS_ACTOR_SCOPE._organisation_type_` is. Void means every type.

default_period.name: default_period
default_period.documentation: The period a relationship written without an end takes.

max_period.name: max_period
max_period.documentation: The longest period a relationship may have.

episode_required.name: episode_required
episode_required.documentation: Whether a relationship the entry covers must name an `episode`; one written without it is refused. Void means false.

invariants.Default_within_max: (default_period /= Void and max_period /= Void) implies default_period.magnitude <= max_period.magnitude

ACCESS_RELATIONSHIP_WRITER.name: ACCESS_RELATIONSHIP_WRITER
ACCESS_RELATIONSHIP_WRITER.documentation: The writers that may state a care relationship to a subject whose EHR is marked at one of the levels named, beside the writers the capabilities already admit.

applies_to.name: applies_to
applies_to.documentation: The writers, any one of which is enough.

confidentialities.name: confidentialities
confidentialities.documentation: The levels, coded in the `HL7_Confidentiality` code system (`N` normal, `R` restricted, `V` very restricted), for which these writers may state a relationship.

ACCESS_CONFLICT_RULE.name: ACCESS_CONFLICT_RULE
ACCESS_CONFLICT_RULE.documentation: A conflict of interest the controller allows through the professional path, for the callers named. An access admitted under it is marked in the access log.

conflict.name: conflict
conflict.documentation: The conflict, coded in the `access conflict` group: `self` (the caller is the subject) or `related` (the caller is related to the subject).

applies_to.name: applies_to
applies_to.documentation: The callers the allowance covers. Void means every professional.

kinships.name: kinships
kinships.documentation: For `related`, the kinship codes the allowance covers. Void means every kinship.

ACCESS_JUSTIFICATION.name: ACCESS_JUSTIFICATION
ACCESS_JUSTIFICATION.documentation: A ground on which the controller admits a caller to an EHR outside its care relationships: a purpose of use the caller declares, with a reason it states, such as a consultation, a second opinion or an emergency. An access that rests on it is marked in the access log with the reason.

purposes.name: purposes
purposes.documentation: The purposes of use, such as the `HL7_ActReason` codes `TREAT`, `ETREAT` or `BTG`, whose declaration invokes the justification.

applies_to.name: applies_to
applies_to.documentation: The callers that may invoke the justification. Void means every caller of kind `professional`.

emergency.name: emergency
emergency.documentation: Whether the justification is an emergency: it then lifts each directive, rule and exclusion whose `_emergency_override_` holds and the steps on sensitivity, confidentiality, care relationship and default, and the access is marked as an emergency access (EHDS Art. 11(5)). Otherwise it stands in for a live care relationship alone.

ACCESS_VALUE_SET.name: ACCESS_VALUE_SET
ACCESS_VALUE_SET.documentation: A value set the controller binds a coded attribute of the package to.

binding.name: binding
binding.documentation: What the value set codes, in the `access value set binding` group: `care_role`, `representation_basis`, `kinship`, `organisation_type` or `care_purpose`.

value_set.name: value_set
value_set.documentation: The canonical URL of the value set on the terminology server.

ACCESS_LOG_RESTRICTION.name: ACCESS_LOG_RESTRICTION
ACCESS_LOG_RESTRICTION.documentation: One restriction of the subject's view of the access log under EHDS Article 9(3). The entries whose accessor is of one of the given kinds are shown to the subject and their representative without the given attributes of the accessor; a reviewer reads the full entry.

accessor_kinds.name: accessor_kinds
accessor_kinds.documentation: The kinds of accessor the restriction applies to, coded in the draft `openehr_access` terminology's `accessor kind` group of the access log, which `ACCESSOR._kind_` is coded in.

withheld.name: withheld
withheld.documentation: The attributes of `ACCESSOR` the subject view withholds, coded in the `access log withheld` group: `accessor_party`, `accessor_provider`, `accessor_roles` or `accessor_groups`.

legal_grounds.name: legal_grounds
legal_grounds.documentation: The provisions of the Member State law that lay the restriction down under EHDS Article 9(3), coded in a terminology the jurisdiction names.

ACCESS_LOG_RETENTION.name: ACCESS_LOG_RETENTION
ACCESS_LOG_RETENTION.documentation: How long the access log keeps each entry, from the date of access, and the floors and ceilings the law binding the controller sets on that period. The controller declares the bounds; the system records them as the grounds of every entry (`ACCESS_RETENTION._grounds_`) and refuses a policy whose period breaks one.

in_union.name: in_union
in_union.documentation: Whether the controller declares itself bound by Regulation (EU) 2025/327, so that its Art. 9(2) keeps each entry at least three years from each date of access.

period.name: period
period.documentation: How long each entry is kept from the date of access; Void keeps it without end.

floors.name: floors
floors.documentation: The minimum periods the law binding the controller sets, each with the provision that sets it.

ceilings.name: ceilings
ceilings.documentation: The maximum periods the law binding the controller sets, each with the provision that sets it.

invariants.Period_union: in_union and period /= Void implies period.magnitude >= P3Y
invariants.Period_floors: floors /= Void and period /= Void implies floors.for_all (f | period.magnitude >= f.period.magnitude)
invariants.Period_ceilings: ceilings /= Void and period /= Void implies ceilings.for_all (c | period.magnitude <= c.period.magnitude)
invariants.Ceilings_floors: ceilings /= Void and floors /= Void implies ceilings.for_all (c | floors.for_all (f | c.period.magnitude >= f.period.magnitude))

ACCESS_RETENTION_BOUND.name: ACCESS_RETENTION_BOUND
ACCESS_RETENTION_BOUND.documentation: One floor or ceiling on how long the access log keeps an entry, with the provision that sets it.

period.name: period
period.documentation: The bound, counted from the date of access.

ground.name: ground
ground.documentation: The provision that sets the bound, coded in a terminology the jurisdiction names, such as the European Legislation Identifier of the act with the subdivision as the code.

VERSIONED_ACCESS_POLICY.name: VERSIONED_ACCESS_POLICY
VERSIONED_ACCESS_POLICY.documentation: Version container for an `ACCESS_POLICY`, committed in contributions with their audit like any other versioned object.

VERSIONED_PARTY_RELATIONSHIP.name: VERSIONED_PARTY_RELATIONSHIP
VERSIONED_PARTY_RELATIONSHIP.documentation: Version container for one `PARTY_RELATIONSHIP` stored on its own, such as a care relationship, committed in contributions with their audit like any other versioned object.
